name: Approved-Parent-Breakdown
note: Deliberately-synthetic fixtures (LIN-3049) for the breakdown-created-subtask exemption in lib/prompts/meta-prompt-template.js. IMPORTANT, per review 8a915947 R2: LIN-APB-pos is a NO-REGRESSION pin, NOT proof the change works — a child carrying a copied approved-plan slice plus `Session fit: fits one session` and a `Plan-review due: no` line already routes to `implement`/`implementation` on UNMODIFIED main (6/6), because the breakdown template writing the slice is what routes it, and no live eval exercises the three meta guards' effect on routing. The three meta guards' only measured routing effect to date is the R1 divergence regression, which LIN-APB-diverged catches; their positive benefit is UNMEASURED here and is to be read via the planned first-routing companion measurement (the engine's own first `/recommend` pick on the first rewritten held child, e.g. LIN-3044). LIN-APB-neg cannot fail: its expect accepts every label observed on both main and the PR, its content is a genuinely small single-surface task (so `implement` is correct under the existing Step-3 exception), and 'no worse than baseline' holds — a thin dispatch-contract child staying in prep remains unmeasured. LIN-APB-diverged is the case that must be zero implement-family: the copied slice cites the parent's approving verdict, but a later comment shows the parent plan revised past that slice, so the gate (and, per R1, the Step-1 and completed-prep guards) must re-derive instead of treating it as settled prep. `research` is included among its accepted outcomes because it is reviewed baseline behaviour (5/6 research on unmodified main) and a legitimate re-derivation when the whole surface moved. Each target is a childless In-Progress leaf (no children/focusedChild) so the descent terminates on it. The deterministic structural half lives in tests/unit/openrouter.test.js and tests/unit/prompt-templates.test.js ('LIN-3049'); this file measures the live routing shape only.

targets.role: no-regression pin: a breakdown child carrying its own copied plan slice + session-fit + plan-review-due:no citing the parent's approving verdict routes to implement/implementation — AND already does so on unmodified main (6/6); this case does NOT isolate the meta guards' effect

non-discriminating control: a breakdown child with a plain acceptance-criteria description and NO recorded Approve (its expect accepts every label seen on both main and the PR, so it cannot fail; a thin dispatch-contract child staying in prep is still unmeasured)

acceptance case: a breakdown child whose copied slice cites the parent's approving verdict, but a later comment shows the parent plan revised past that slice — the gate (and the Step-1/completed-prep guards) must re-derive on visible divergence; acceptance criterion is ZERO implement-family (research is accepted: reviewed baseline 5/6 research on main)

issue.title: Token exchange: mint one scoped child proxy token
issue.description:
## Slice of the approved parent plan (LIN-PARENT)

**Source of truth: LIN-PARENT's approved Implementation Plan and its approving plan-review — do not redesign this surface; re-ground it against the current code and stop to recommend re-planning if it has drifted.**

- **Files/surfaces:** the token exchange in `routes/proxy-token.js` (mint the child token) and the child-token record shape in `lib/token-record.js` (record the parent token id).
- **Approach:** extend the existing working-token exchange so a working token can mint exactly one scoped child token, inheriting scope and ownership, and record the parent token id on the child for the audit trail.
- **Testing strategy:** unit-cover inheritance and the single-use bootstrap invariant.

**Session fit: fits one session**

**Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-PARENT's approving plan-review (comment 48be9b95, rev 3)**

**Grounding:** `71688a42`.
